title: Quillfield Pharma onprem triage notes
content:
Context: quick working notes from kickoff call with Quillfield Pharma (Jan 11). They’re evaluating a Private deployment for inference in an air-gapped/regulatory environment. This doc is a rough capture of requirements, immediate technical risks, and next actions. Use as a shared scratchpad for eng + SE until we have a formal SOW.

Attendees (as captured):
- Dr. Leena Kapoor (Quillfield) - Head of Data & ML
- Tom Morales (Quillfield) - Infra lead / SRE
- Priya Singh (Quillfield) - Compliance
- Maya Chen (Redwood) - Solutions Eng (owner)
- Evan Patel (Redwood) - Private Deploys eng

High-level ask:
- Host LLM inference entirely inside Quillfield data center (no outbound model data allowed), optionally with a private Redwood control plane air-gapped or via managed proxy.
- Audit trail and tamper-evident logs for all API calls (21 CFR Part 11 + HIPAA posture).
- Ability to pin specific model versions and roll back quickly.
- Throughput target: baseline 100 qps for short-chat workloads, burst to 250 qps; p95 latency target <= 300ms for 128-token responses.
- Determinism/quality checks for hallucination-sensitive outputs (structured extraction tasks).

Environment notes / constraints from Tom:
- Rack-level GPUs available: mixed fleet (2x A100 40GB, 4x A10 24GB); no H100s currently.
- Network: strict outbound firewall; only allow specific egress to Redwood control plane IPs via a jump/proxy.
- No public internet access for inference nodes in final state; initial PoC can allow limited outbound.
- Existing on-prem KMS (Thales) and HSM available; want Redwood to integrate with customer KMS for model encryption keys.

Security & compliance priorities (from Priya / Leena):
- FIPS-compliant crypto for key material in transit and at rest.
- Full request/response logging with immutable audit indexing. Need ability to export logs for e-discovery.
- Role-based access and separation: dev/test vs prod tenants.
- Data retention controls + automated purge for ephemeral tokens.
- Validate Redwood “private” instrumentation doesn't leak prompts to hosted services.

Technical design constraints / gotchas to watch:
- Air-gap mode: Redwood Private has an on-prem bundle but we need an offline installer + signed model bundles. Verify that the control plane can be operated in an offline mode or via a one-way sync.
- Quantization: customer wants INT8 to save GPU memory, but model accuracy must be validated against extraction eval. Plan explicit eval sweep (see next steps).
- KV cache effectiveness: workload is repetitive clinical extraction, good opportunity for prefix/KV cache to reduce cost. Need to measure average prefix length distribution.
- Cold starts: A100 nodes may have slow first-token spikes for large models; propose warm-pool strategy + continuous batching.
- Proxy/NAT: customer proxy may rewrite headers and terminate TLS. Validate TLS origination points and cert chain; they require mutual-TLS between control plane and onprem agent.
- Audit artifacts: log size will be large (full payloads). Discuss log sampling vs full retention for compliance team.

Evaluation & quality plan:
- Build a 300-item prompt set (Quillfield-provided) focused on structured extraction from clinical notes + hallucination tests.
- Baseline run on open-llm-1.2 / readability model + quantized variants. Track precision/recall and hallucination rate.
- Define regression thresholds (e.g., >2% drop in extraction-F1 triggers hold on rollout).

Pilot scope (suggested):
- Phase 0: PoC (1 week) with limited outbound to Redwood control plane. Deploy a single A100 node, Redwood onprem agent, sample model (small-ish) to validate connectivity, KMS handshake, and canary traffic.
- Phase 1: Local-only pilot (3 weeks). Air-gapped install with signed bundles, basic logging, run eval set, collect metrics.
- Phase 2: Scale (4-6 weeks). Add batching, KV cache, production routing, canary rollouts. Enable RBAC and audit export.

Immediate open questions (need answers from Quillfield / follow-up):
- Which models are they legally required to avoid? Any third-party licensed models that are disallowed?
- Exact retention window required for API logs (Priya to confirm).
- Do they require continuous attestation of image integrity (SCAP) and vulnerability scanning as part of SOW?
- Will the onprem network allow inbound connections from Redwood support for remote debugging, or must we use a VPN/jump wholly under customer control?

Action items & owners (rough):
- Maya: produce a short PoC runbook + connectivity checklist (due Jan 14).
- Evan: validate offline installer flow and create list of supported GPUs + known perf deltas (due Jan 16).
- Tom (Quillfield): provide sample clinical prompt set and retention policy doc (due Jan 17).
- Priya (Quillfield): confirm compliance must-haves (FIPS parts, retention) and share contact in legal for drafting addendum (due Jan 15).
- Maya/Evan: schedule an on-site install dry-run (2 hour) with Quillfield infra team for week of Jan 20.

Notes / informal observations:
- Leena is explicitly worried about hallucination-caused downstream regulatory risk; emphasize Redwood Optimize eval hooks and rollout gates during next call.
- Tom seems open to hybrid approach: local inference + periodic signed telemetry bundles to Redwood for SaaS analytics in a tightly controlled channel. We should propose an encrypted, signed bundle upload rather than streaming telemetry.
- Compliance asked about evidence for signed model provenance; we should prepare artifact list (signed model manifest, checksum, builder provenance).

Next call agenda (proposed):
1) Walk PoC runbook & connectivity checklist (Maya)
2) KMS/HSM integration approach and mutual-TLS handshake details (Evan/Tom)
3) Pilot eval design & baseline metrics (Leena/Evan)
4) Compliance addendum checklist and evidence requirements (Priya)

Longer-term notes:
- If pilot successful, customer will likely want a Reserved Dedicated contract for 3x A100-equivalent capacity. Pre-authorize capacity planning and a pricing sketch.
- Consider pre-creating an “offline model bundle” workflow in our private deploy docs to speed future talks.

End of scratchpad. Use this as ephemeral working doc; will move to Confluence once requirements are stable.

Latest edits: added pilot phases and owners (Maya, 2025-01-15).
